entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11856"/><div sID="gen21440" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11856"/><hi type="bold">7. the place--</hi>that is, "behold the place of My throne"--the place on which your thoughts have so much dwelt (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.1-Isa.2.3">Is 2:1-3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.3.17">Jr 3:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.16-Zech.14.20">Zec 14:16-20</reference>; Mal 3:1). God from the first claimed to be their King politically as well as religiously: and He had resisted their wish to have a human king, as implying a rejection of Him as the proper Head of the state. Even when He yielded to their wish, it was with a protest against their king ruling except as His vicegerent. When Messiah shall reign at Jerusalem, He shall then first realize the original idea of the theocracy, with its at once divine and human king reigning in righteousness over a people all righteous (<reference osisRef="Ezek.43.12">Eze 43:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.52.1">Is 52:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.54.13">54:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.60.21">60:21</reference>). <div eID="gen21440" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 7. the place-- that is, "behold the place of My throne"--the place on which your thoughts have so much dwelt ( Is 2:1-3 ; Jr 3:17 ; Zec 14:16-20 ; Mal 3:1). God from the first claimed to be their King politically as well as religiously: and He had resisted their wish to have a human king, as implying a rejection of Him as the proper Head of the state. Even when He yielded to their wish, it was with a protest against their king ruling except as His vicegerent. When Messiah shall reign at Jerusalem, He shall then first realize the original idea of the theocracy, with its at once divine and human king reigning in righteousness over a people all righteous ( Eze 43:12 ; Is 52:1 ; 54:13 ; 60:21 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11857"/><div sID="gen21441" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11857"/><hi type="bold">9. carcasses of their kings--</hi>It is supposed that some of their idolatrous kings were buried within the bounds of Solomon's temple [Henderson]. Rather, "the carcasses of their idols," here called "kings," as having had lordship over them in past times (<reference osisRef="Isa.26.13">Is 26:13</reference>); but henceforth Jehovah, alone their rightful lord, shall be their king, and the idols that had been their "king" would appear but as "carcasses." Hence these defunct kings are associated with the "high places" in <reference osisRef="Ezek.43.7">Eze 43:7</reference> [Fairbairn]. <reference osisRef="Lev.26.30">Le 26:30</reference> and <reference osisRef="Jer.16.18">Jr 16:18</reference>, confirm this. Manasseh had built altars in the courts of the temple to the host of heaven (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.21.5">2Ki 21:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.23.6">23:6</reference>).<div eID="gen21441" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen21442" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">I will dwell in the midst ... for ever--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Rev.21.3">Re 21:3</reference>). <div eID="gen21442" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 9. carcasses of their kings-- It is supposed that some of their idolatrous kings were buried within the bounds of Solomon's temple [Henderson]. Rather, "the carcasses of their idols," here called "kings," as having had lordship over them in past times ( Is 26:13 ); but henceforth Jehovah, alone their rightful lord, shall be their king, and the idols that had been their "king" would appear but as "carcasses." Hence these defunct kings are associated with the "high places" in Eze 43:7 [Fairbairn]. Le 26:30 and Jr 16:18 , confirm this. Manasseh had built altars in the courts of the temple to the host of heaven ( 2Ki 21:5 ; 23:6 ). I will dwell in the midst ... for ever-- ( Re 21:3 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv11859"/><div sID="gen21444" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv11859"/><hi type="bold">12. whole ... most holy--</hi>This superlative, which had been used exclusively of the holy of holies (<reference osisRef="Exod.26.34">Ex 26:34</reference>), was now to characterize the entire building. This all-pervading sanctity was to be "the law of the (whole) house," as distinguished from the Levitical law, which confined the peculiar sanctity to a single apartment of it. <div eID="gen21444" type="x-p"/>
